subject: Discovery recap: Data privacy & logging requirements (Acme Corp)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acme-corp.com>, Bob Li <bob.li@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Data privacy & logging requirements (Acme Corp)

Hi Alice / Bob —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Pain points / goals:
- Primary goal: bring LLM-powered customer support assistant live without sending PII to any shared multi-tenant endpoints.
- Current stack: in-house vector DB (self-hosted), event pipeline to S3, AWS KMS for keys.
- Concerns: PII discovery/redaction, retention limits for raw request/response logs, and auditable access to inference logs for incident response.

Success criteria for POC (what Acme will measure):
1) No customer-identifying PII persisted beyond agreed retention window (default ask: 90 days) unless flagged/consented.
2) Audit logs capturing request id, model variant, top-level metadata (no raw PII unless explicitly redacted), and admin access logs retained for 12 months.
3) Ability to run field-level redaction and downstream replay for debugging without exposing PII to engineers.

What Redwood can offer / proposed approach:
- Private deployment option (VPC) or Dedicated with per-customer isolated storage and optional request-level redaction.
- Configurable retention for request/response logs; default retention policy can be set to 90 days for PII-containing traffic.
- Audit log export to your S3 with bucket-level encryption + KMS integration.
- Optional client-side tokenization pattern for extra assurance.

Immediate next steps:
1) You to share the security questionnaire you mentioned (attach if easiest).
2) We’ll send a short SOC 2 summary and a proposed redaction/retention configuration for review (ETA: tomorrow).
3) Schedule a 30-min call with your security lead to walk the config and any contract redlines.

Attachment stub: acme-security-questions.xlsx (please attach the questionnaire or paste answers inline).

If I missed anything, flag it and I’ll update. Thanks — looking forward to aligning on the POC scope.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0198
https://www.redwoodinference.com

Marissa —

Thanks for the thorough recap. That aligns with what we discussed. Attaching the security questionnaire you requested (acme-security-questions.xlsx). A few clarifications from our side: 
- Retention: 90 days for anything that contains customer PII is our baseline but may be shortened depending on contract/legal review.
- Audit logs: we need immutable logs for admin actions and data access, preferably shipped to our S3 with write-once lifecycle.
- Redaction: field-level redaction is ideal. If you support client-side tokenization that helps.

I’m copying our security team in case they want to join the call — they’ll likely ask about HSM/KMS topology and whether Redwood processes raw request content in any shared control plane.

Thanks,
Alice Chen
Head of Infrastructure, Acme Corp
alice.chen@acme-corp.com

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Data privacy & logging requirements (Acme Corp)

Hi all —

Attached is a short SOC 2 summary and a proposed redaction + retention config for the POC (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf). High-level responses to the questionnaire we received: 
- Do you store raw request/response content in shared systems? No — for Dedicated/Private we isolate customer artifacts; for Hosted API we support configurable KV-caching and can enable request-level redaction prior to any persistent storage.
- KMS/HSM: We integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS/Azure KeyVault) for at-rest encryption of exported logs; HSM support for key material is available for Private deployments.
- Audit logs: We can export immutable admin and request metadata to your S3 with server-side encryption + bucket policies.
- Redaction: Field-level redaction rules (regex-based and named fields) supported; we also provide a client-side SDK for tokenization if you prefer no raw PII leaves your environment.

Proposed POC plan:
1) 2-week sandbox in Dedicated mode with log export to your staging S3.
2) Retention configured to 90 days for PII-containing logs; non-PII telemetry retained 180 days.
3) Security walkthrough with your team (30 min) — can we schedule for tomorrow afternoon?

Attachment stub: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

Thanks — looping in Dev (SE) to cover technical setup and network requirements.

Best,
Marissa

Hi Marissa / Dev —

Appreciate the summary. A few follow-ups before the walkthrough: 
1) Retention max: we need the ability to enforce a 90-day max for any PII-containing logs; please confirm deletion workflows and proof-of-deletion for the POC.
2) Redaction: field-level redaction is required for at-rest copies. Any debug replay mechanisms must operate on tokenized data unless explicit business consent is recorded.
3) Auditability: admin access logs must be immutable and retained for 12 months. We expect a signed export (or integrity check) on daily archives.
4) KMS: for Private deployments we will require HSM-backed keys and proof that key material never leaves our control plane.

Please send the proposed POC config and any implementation notes on deletion proofs prior to the call.

Thanks,
Acme Security Team
security@acme-corp.com
